'''Gérard Henri de Vaucouleurs''' ({{IPA|fr|ʒeʁaʁ ɑ̃ʁi də vokulœʁ}}; 25 April 1918 &ndash; 7 October 1995)<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Burbidge |first=E. Margaret |date=2002 |title=GÉRARD DE VAUCOULEURS 1918–1995 |url=https://www.nasonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/de-vaucouleurs-gerard.pdf |journal=Biographical Memoirs |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |volume=82 |via=National Academy of Sciences Online}}</ref><ref name=nyt19951011>{{cite news| first1=Robert McG. Jr. | last1=Thomas | date=October 11, 1995 | title=Gerard de Vaucouleurs, 77, Galactic Astronomer, Is Dead | newspaper =The New York Times | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1995/10/11/us/gerard-de-vaucouleurs-77-galactic-astronomer-is-dead.html | access-date=2012-02-21 }}</ref> was a French [[astronomer]] best known for his studies of galaxies.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Gerard de Vaucouleurs {{!}} McDonald Observatory |url=https://mcdonaldobservatory.org/news/gallery/gerard-de-vaucouleurs |access-date=2023-06-17 |website=mcdonaldobservatory.org}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Gérard de Vaucouleurs was born on April 25, 1918 in Paris, he took the maiden name of his mother as his last name.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Burbidge |first=Geoffrey |date=30 November 1995 |title=Gérard de Vaucouleurs (1918–95) |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/378440a0.pdf |journal=Nature |volume=378 |issue=6556 |pages=440|doi=10.1038/378440a0 |bibcode=1995Natur.378..440B |s2cid=46470185 }}</ref> He had an early interest in [[amateur astronomy]] and received his undergraduate degree in 1939 at the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]] in that city.

After military service in World War II, he resumed his pursuit of astronomy. He was married to fellow astronomer [[Antoinette de Vaucouleurs]] on October 31, 1944, and the couple would frequently collaborate on astronomical research.<ref name="Antoinette2008">{{cite web | title=In Memoriam: Antoinette de Vaucouleurs, 1921-1987 | date=October 13, 2008 | publisher=The University of Texas at Austin | url=http://www.as.utexas.edu/lectures/adv.html }}</ref>

He was fluent in English and spent 1949-51 in England and 1951&ndash;57 in Australia at [[Mount Stromlo Observatory]]. He was at [[Lowell Observatory]] in [[Arizona]] from 1957-1958 and at [[Harvard College Observatory|Harvard]] from 1958-60.

In 1960 he was appointed to the [[University of Texas at Austin]], where he spent the rest of his career. He was one of the first five faculty in the newly formed astronomy department there.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Antoinette2008" /> His wife Antoinette died in 1987. In 1995 he died of a heart attack in his home in Austin at the age of 77.<ref name="nyt19951011" /> At the time of his death he had a second wife named Elysabeth.<ref name="nyt19951011" /><ref name=":1" />

== Research ==
His earliest work had concerned the planet Mars and while at Harvard he used telescope observations from 1909 to 1958 to study the [[Areography|areographic]] coordinates of features on the surface of Mars.<ref>{{Cite book| last = de Vaucouleurs | first = Gerard | date = 1963  | chapter = Precision Mapping of Mars | title = La Physique des Planètes; Communications Présentées au Onzième Colloque International d'Astrophysique tenu à Liège, les 9, 10 et 11 Juillet 1962. | series = Liège International Astrophysical Colloquia |publisher=Institut d'Astrophysique Cointe-Solessin |location=Belgique | volume = 11| pages = 369–385 | bibcode = 1963LIACo..11..369D }}</ref>  His later work focused on the study of [[galaxy|galaxies]] and he co-authored the ''Third Reference Catalogue of Bright Galaxies'' with his wife Antoinette (1921-1987), a fellow UT Austin astronomer and lifelong collaborator.<ref name=Antoinette2008/>

His specialty included reanalyzing Hubble and Sandage's galaxy atlas and recomputing the distance measurements utilizing a method of averaging many different kinds of metrics such as luminosity, the diameters of ring galaxies, brightest star clusters, etc., in a method he called "spreading the risks." During the 1950s he promoted the idea that galactic clusters are grouped into superclusters.<ref name=nyt19951011/>

The ''[[Galaxy morphological classification|de Vaucouleurs modified Hubble sequence]]'' is a widely used variant of the standard [[Hubble sequence]].

De Vaucouleurs was awarded the [[Henry Norris Russell Lectureship]] by the [[American Astronomical Society]] in 1988. He was awarded the [[Prix Jules Janssen]] of the [[Société astronomique de France]] (Astronomical Society of France) in the same year. He and his wife and longtime collaborator, Antoinette, together produced 400 research and technical papers, 20 books and 100 articles for laymen.<ref name=nyt19951011/>
